name: Aetosauroides
sum: Aetosauroides is an extinct aetosaur from the Late Triassic of South America, one of the oldest members of its group.
wsnote: Most individuals were about 1.3 m long; one large individual reached 2.4 m (histology suggests an age of about 23 years); males may have reached about 2 m if the sexual dimorphism suggested in the literature is real.
holotype: Not stated in the sources consulted for this draft; see the original description (Casamiquela 1960).
material: Several individuals of A. scagliai from the Ischigualasto Formation (Argentina) and the Santa Maria Formation (Brazil), including a skull and postcranial material used in studies of intraspecific variation.
biology: Histology of a large individual suggests it lived about 23 years; sexual maturity was probably reached at about 1 m, and sexual dimorphism has been proposed, with males reaching around 2 m.
author: Casamiquela 1960
